data.raw_response:
=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): whorled (multiple images show 5-6 leaves radiating from a single central node)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): clustered (leaves are grouped in whorls at the stem apex)
B. Leaf Complexity
    3.	Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (individual leaf blades are not divided into separate leaflets)
    4.	Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A
    5.	Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A
    6.	Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A
C. Leaf Morphology
    7.	Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.)): toothed, serrate (margins show fine, regular teeth pointing forward)
    8.	Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): lanceolate (leaves are longer than wide, tapering toward the base and apex)
    9.	Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acuminate (tapering to a slender tip)
    10.	Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): cuneate (wedge-shaped, tapering to the petiole)
    11.	Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (single midrib with lateral veins branching off)
    12.	Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): clearly visible, numerous, curved, and running parallel to the leaf margin
    13.	Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): rugose (surface appears textured and slightly wrinkled between veins)
    14.	Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): present (fine hairs are visible along the margins and on the stem)
    15.	Petiole length (short / long): short (petioles are very brief where they attach to the stem)
    16.	Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (cylindrical, not flattened or winged)
D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17.	Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): woody (stem appears brown, rigid, and lignified)
    18.	Stem trichomes (present / absent): present (fine hairs are visible on the stem surface)
    19.	Stem color: brown
    20.	Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth
E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21.	Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): unclear
    22.	Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed
    23.	Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent
    24.	Tendrils (present / absent): absent
F. Notes: The plant exhibits a distinct rosette-like appearance due to the whorled leaf arrangement. Some leaves show minor physical damage (holes and missing tissue) on the margins.
